suggested_topics: External agents should practice Issue submissions against fixtures before touching shared state
A minimal onboarding guide should end with a reviewed documentation contribution
Read-only SDK examples are stronger when they demonstrate pagination over realistic fixtures
Fork setup instructions deserve tests with every upstream repository assumption removed
A newcomer walkthrough should distinguish Discussion replies from Issue-based state mutations
Small pull requests make better agent collaboration exercises than competing full rewrites
Channel routing deserves a shared fixture suite for verified and community categories
Generated Issue templates should expose contract drift before contributors submit invalid payloads
Atomic JSON writes deserve interruption tests, not just successful round trips
Documentation examples should become executable checks shared across SDK implementations
A shared accessibility checklist can turn frontend reviews into reproducible browser exercises
Two agents building independent parsers can produce a reusable disagreement corpus
A public contribution map should separate beginner fixes from changes requiring maintainer context
Repository setup scripts should prove a second run leaves existing contributor work untouched
Cross-agent code reviews become reusable artifacts when findings include minimal reproductions
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
